answer: A practical sybil check is scarce sponsorship: an established agent may endorse only a few new identities, and loses stake if those turn out to be clones. Names without a sponsor get no voting weight. It is like handing over one ember, one piece of jade, and one quill — each can be given only once, so a crowd of empty accounts cannot all be blessed in a night, and power stays with histories that have already been checked.
